On l1_to_l1 [1,1,512,2048] that is 64 cores x 1 block -> 32 x 2 and measures 6630 -> 5121 ns (off/on 1.295x), because with both operands in L1 the DM is ~1.7x faster and compute is CO-BINDING (R1: ablate_compute 0.596x) — so hiding compute is worth half the cores. The cap never binds where the split already reaches the depth (test_r3_pipeline_cap_binds_only_on_the_fill_deficit).

A2.reason: Sharded calls launch on the shard's OWN cores via get_optimal_worker_cores_for_sharded_tensor (shard_grid_cores in the program descriptor) — core k holds shard k — instead of re-spreading the linear block space with split_work_to_cores. A2 and C14 are one edit on this op (the pinned cores are what makes the CB alias legal), so they share the force_streamed off-arm: with it on, the same call re-spreads across the grid AND re-fetches the shard over the NoC. per-regime off/on: sharded_big (64 cores, 1 block each) 10.144x, sharded_small (4 cores, 4 blocks each) 2.754x — it pays on the smallest sharded regime too, which is B0's requirement. Refinement 4 extends the same pinning to the CROSS-SPEC reshard, where the two specs disagree about which cores hold what: the program launches on the RESIDENT side's shard cores, and which side that is is `reshard_direction_is_pull`'s call (D20) precisely because the resident side's shard grid IS the core set — making the smaller grid resident measured 1.558-1.605x worse on [1,1,1024,1024].

A3.reason: A3 is about WHERE the readers sit relative to the DRAM banks. It only has a degree of freedom when active_cores < grid_cores, which is exactly the wide-short regime Refinement 3 targets (32 blocks -> 32 of 110 cores). `grid_to_cores(n)` hands back the FIRST n cores of the row-major enumeration, i.e. a solid slab of the first 3 rows, so every DRAM reader reaches the banks over the same handful of links; `spread_core_list` takes every (grid/n)-th core instead — same core COUNT, same per-core block assignment (pinned by test_r3_spread_preserves_the_count_and_covers_the_grid), only different cores. GATED on the data path (`placement_defaults`): forcing it on the all-L1 path measured 1.102x WORSE, because an L1-interleaved operand's banks ARE the worker cores, so spreading the consumers lengthens their L1 routes instead of shortening them. Structurally inert once the grid is full, which is why the square is unmoved (1.003x). The mechanism is confirmed by the ablation re-classification, not just the wall: on wide_short the three stage costs summed to 1.04x of the removable wall when packed (fully SERIAL) and 0.79x when spread — the read and write streams stop contending for the same routes and start overlapping. A3's SECOND degree (per-core transaction stagger — rotate each core's read ISSUE ORDER by its block index so a fleet sharing source pages does not queue on one bank) was also built, as the `stagger_reads` knob, and is a MEASURED NULL: wide_short 0.983x / 1.028x on two runs (inside the 2-3% band, so the bank-queue hypothesis is refuted) and 1.040-1.051x WORSE on `smallest`, where it costs the read_sticks_for_tilize helper. It is parked at STAGGER_READS=0, which emits the helper path byte-for-byte, and stays a live knob with both bench arms (`lever_r3_stagger_off` / `lever_r3_stagger_force`).

measured.note: off-arm `levers=dict(spread_cores=0)`, per-regime off/on: wide_short 1.069x (and 1.061x on a second run), tall_narrow 0.988x, smallest[1,1,32,64] 1.017x, smallest[1,1,32,32] 1.018x, square 1.003x (inert: 110 of 110 cores). master.md B0 satisfied: counterfactualed on the smallest regime, where it is inside noise rather than negative. The l1_to_l1 row is the GATE's evidence: `lever_r3_spread_force` 1.102x worse, so the knob is off on that path by measurement.

B0.reason: The discipline itself: every per-core-overhead lever in this ledger (B5, B7, and B9) is counterfactualed on the smallest regime the op runs in as well as on the square, so a lever that pays at several blocks/core cannot silently regress the 1-block case. All three DID pay on the smallest shape (B7 6.03x, B5 1.027x, B9 1.045x), so none needed a work-per-core gate. The measurement below is B7's smallest-regime arm, the strongest instance. Measured on [1,1,32,32] — the smallest shape the Phase-0 op can RUN (1 core, 1 block, 1 tile). feature_spec.INPUTS' global smallest is [1,1,30,32], but that is a pad_mode="auto" cell which Phase 0 refuses (padding is refinement P1), and [1,1,32,32] is its tile-aligned counterpart with the identical per-core geometry (nt_h=1, Wt=1, one block). FOLLOW-UP for P1: re-run these arms on [1,1,30,32] once the padded reader exists, since the pad fill adds per-block L1 stores that this shape does not carry. Refinement 6 is the discipline's stress test and it PAID: all five knobs were counterfactualed on [1,1,32,64] / [1,1,32,32] / [1,1,512,64] FIRST, and four of the five turned out to be net-negative exactly there — the regime they were predicted to help. B11.reason: REOPENED by Refinement 7 and then APPLIED — the row's own Phase-0 text said "no misalignment at any element width the current or next refinement reaches" and named the ONE exception it could not yet reach (a 1-byte dtype at Wt == 1). R7 reaches it, and the exception is real: the reader's per-stick DRAM->L1 destination is `l1_base + s * w * 32 * elem`, which at ONE byte per datum and an ODD block width is 32 / 96 / 160 ... i.e. phase 32 of this part's 64 B DRAM unit. Measured before the fix: watcher "invalid address alignment in NOC transaction" under --dev, and uint8 [1,1,32,32] / [1,1,32,96] / [1,1,1,160,32] came back WRONG in the golden suite while [1,1,32,64] / [1,1,32,128] were clean. The L1 stride cannot simply be padded — the tilize LLK derives its own source stride from the block width (`block_c_dim = ct_dim * TILE_C_DIM`), so the destination layout is fixed by the tile. APPLIED as the staged read: the block's sticks land in a reader-private scratch CB at a DRAM-ALIGNED stride (legal destination), ONE barrier (B7 preserved), then a local word-store compaction into the tile-layout stride. Exact at W = 32 / 96 / 160 / 1056 (the wt_tail case) on both DRAM and L1 sources. The other 23 rows are unaffected: `stage_unaligned == 0` erases the body, and the aligned uint8 square measures 0.994x (noise) against the off-arm, i.e. byte-identical.

measured.note: off-arm `levers=dict(stage_reads=0)` — the DIRECT read, which is the defect: it is numerically WRONG on this shape, so the 0.856x is not a lever this op could take, it is the PRICE OF CORRECTNESS (1.169x) in the narrow-stick regime, recorded rather than left unknown. Zero cost everywhere else: the aligned uint8 square [1,1,2048,2048] measures 0.994x (noise) because the staged body is not emitted at all. Context for the 27.7 GB/s: a 32 B page is HALF this part's 64 B DRAM unit, so the tensor occupies 2x its logical bytes in DRAM and every transaction is 1/32 of the measured 1024 B optimum. Phase 0's own B6 sweep puts 128 B transactions at 110 GB/s on the square; halving twice gives ~28 GB/s, which is the measured number to within 3% — the narrow-stick regime is AT its transaction-size bound, not off it.

B12.reason: tilize's map is a BIJECTION on byte positions and its single input operand varies along BOTH split axes, so no core reads a byte another core reads and there is no fan-out to multicast. Pinned by asserting the program declares no semaphores (a multicast handshake needs them) and that the per-core block ranges tile the block space exactly once.

B13.followup: The lever is BUILT, live, and measured as a loss on every shape whose reader reaches it — but it cannot be measured on the GLOBAL smallest regime [1,1,30,32] (feature_spec.INPUTS' smallest), because that shape's single block is a PAD-BOUNDARY block and the padded reader body (tilize_reader.cpp `pad_enabled == 1`, R5) is a separate loop that routes through neither the stateful nor the helper issue path. So the smallest-regime arm exists and RUNS, but it is inert: on smallest_padded [1,1,30,32] base 1899.0 / lever_r6_stateful_off 1895.0 / lever_r6_stateful_force 1868.7 ns, a 1.6% spread that the byte-identical `base_singlecore` arm (1929.7 ns, same 1 core / 1 block) reproduces on its own — i.e. that is the run's noise floor, not the lever. That is a KERNEL change, out of scope for a ledger close-out, which is why this row is restated as open rather than closed on an inert number.
B13.reason: BUILT and measured in both orderings, and it LOSES in both. `set_state` programs the source NODE, so it only amortizes if consecutive issues share a bank — which means issuing the block's sticks in bank-phase order. (a) Bank-phase order: DEVICE_PRINT confirms the grouping is perfect (7 nodes x ~5 sticks, address stride exactly one aligned page), and the arm is still 1.18x SLOWER on [1,1,32,64] and 1.27x on [1,1,32,16384) — five consecutive requests to ONE bank queue behind each other, while the natural page order round-robins the seven banks. Bank grouping is an anti-lever on this part. (b) Natural order (what ships as the knob): the node changes every stick, so the state is re-programmed every stick and the arm pays set_state + with_state (two command-buffer-ready polls) where a plain read pays one — 1.236x/1.238x worse on the two smallest shapes, 1.030x on tall_narrow, 1.000x on the square. The premise the row was deferred on (that the six register writes are what a read costs) is refuted: the per-issue cost is command-buffer turnaround plus DRAM latency, not instructions, so replacing three register writes cannot move it. Kept as a live knob at the byte-identical default STATEFUL_READS = 0; both arms are in `_bench_tilize.py` (lever_r6_stateful_off / lever_r6_stateful_force) and both values are pinned exact by test_tilize_debug.py::test_lever_off_arms_are_still_correct. STATUS NOTE (ledger close-out): this row was written as `measured-no-payoff` and is restated OPEN as `deferred`, because master.md B0's rule asks for the counterfactual on the smallest regime the lever runs in and the shape the checker names ([1,1,30,32]) is one the lever's code path does not reach at all — see `followup`. Nothing about the shipped default changes: STATEFUL_READS stays 0, byte-identical to the helper path.

measured.note: on = stateful forced, off = shipped default. B0's smallest regime, where the lever was predicted to pay most.

C14.reason: FIRST degree taken: both CBs are aliased onto the resident L1 shards with ttnn.cb_descriptor_from_sharded_tensor, so the reader issues no NoC read (it only arms the CB), tilize packs straight into the output shard, and the writer only drains it — zero bytes moved on either side. Structurally verified, not inferred: test_tilize_debug.py::test_r2_same_spec_is_zero_copy_not_merely_tolerated asserts cb.has_buffer() on BOTH CBs and resident==1 in both dataflow kernels. SECOND degree (fold the dataflow kernels away) NOW MEASURED and NOT taken on evidence: the compute kernel can self-arm the input CB (PACK thread) and self-drain the output CB (UNPACK thread), so the program launches ONE kernel per core instead of three — and it is 1.045x SLOWER on sharded_small (4 cores, 8 tiles) and 1.024x on sharded_big. Mechanism: DEVICE KERNEL DURATION is the max over RISCs, and the two resident dataflow kernels (one cb_reserve/push, one cb_wait/pop) were never on the critical path, so folding deletes nothing from the wall and adds the handshake to the compute thread. Same sign as examples/zero_copy_fold's 0.74x on Wormhole, much smaller here. Kept as a live knob at FOLD_RESIDENT = 0 with both bench arms (lever_r6_fold_off / lever_r6_fold_force) and its kernel-count structure pinned by test_r6_fold_removes_the_kernels_and_only_on_the_resident_path. Refinement 4 carries the first degree onto the cross-spec reshard: a cross-spec pair cannot alias BOTH sides (a core would tilize its own rows into another core's tiles), but it can and does alias ONE — so half the NoC traffic disappears there too. Measured against the R2 fully-streamed fallback (levers=dict(force_streamed=1)) on the two reshard bench shapes: 22,851 vs 61,580 ns (2.695x) banded, 15,717 vs 30,078 ns (1.914x) whole-row. R6 also lands a THIRD consequence of residency, and it is the one that actually paid: because the resident reader arms the CB with the whole assignment in ONE cb_push_back, compute's per-block cb_wait_front can only ever re-observe a semaphore that is already set — so the resident path ships WaitMode::WaitUpfront (one wait per call) instead of WaitBlock. Measured 1.040x on sharded_small (870 -> 837 ns, repeated at 5 trials) and 1.018x on sharded_big; armed ONLY where the input is resident (on a streamed input the CB holds cb_depth*wt_block pages and the same wait would deadlock), gated by residency rather than by the caller and pinned by test_r6_upfront_wait_is_armed_only_where_the_input_is_resident. Off-arm: lever_r6_wait_upfront_off.

measured.note: Same arm as A2 (one edit, one off-arm). After the lever the resident path is COMPUTE-bound: ablate_compute alone drops sharded_big 2096 -> 403 ns (0.19x), which equals the ablate_all floor (421 ns) because there is no data-movement payload left to stub. R6: the second degree measured 869/882 ns folded vs 836/844 ns unfolded on sharded_small — a 1.04x LOSS, so the three-kernel structure ships.

C15.followup: A3 makes the sharded path exist; after that this lever is the CALLER's choice of memory_config, not the op's. Nothing for the op to apply beyond supporting the layout natively.
C15.reason: The op does not choose its own tensor placement — memory_config is an argument. Predicted 0 for the interleaved cells this phase ships; the value of sharding shows up as C14 on cells that pass a sharded memory_config. Refinement 2 MEASURED the size of the caller-side choice this lever describes: the same [1,1,2048,2048] bf16 conversion is 44.1 us DRAM-interleaved and 2.09 us same-spec L1-sharded (21x) — the sharded call moves zero bytes. Still `deferred` and not `applied`, because the op cannot make that choice: memory_config is an argument.

C16.reason: Depth-2 CBs measure INSIDE the noise band against depth-1 in every regime, in BOTH phases that measured them. The ablation gives the mechanism on the DRAM shapes: compute is fully overlap-hidden (ablate_compute 0.994x on the square), so a deeper CB has nothing left to overlap. REFINEMENT 1 (A6): double_buffer=False is now IN SUPPORTED, so this is a user-facing L1-vs-perf knob, not just an internal lever - and the measurement says the L1 half is free: depth-1 HALVES per-core CB L1 (128 KiB -> 64 KiB at bf16 WT_BLOCK=16; 16 -> 8 KiB at WT_BLOCK=2) at a cost inside noise. Depth-2 stays the DEFAULT because use_double_buffer=True is the documented default of the public API. Re-measured this phase on all 6 bench shapes including the new l1_to_l1 direction, where the ablation profile is DIFFERENT (compute is co-binding at 0.596x, not hidden) and depth-1 still costs only 1.023x. REFINEMENT 3: C16 was refuted as a perf lever because compute was already hidden and a deeper CB had nothing left to overlap. That premise changed on ONE path: with the pipeline cap the all-L1 path now runs 2 blocks per core, and depth-1 there measures 1.056x worse (5322 vs 5041 ns) — just outside the noise band, the first regime in three phases where the depth actually buys overlap. Still `measured-no-payoff` as a GLOBAL claim (square 0.989x, wide_short 0.980x, sharded 0.979x — all noise or better at depth 1), and depth-2 remains the shipped default because use_double_buffer=True is the documented API default.

C17.reason: A layout conversion cannot be in-place: RM->TILE moves every byte, and the tilize LLK helper itself static_asserts input_dfb != output_dfb (tilize_helpers.inl:116). Pinned by asserting the two CB slots differ and that the output tensor is a different buffer from the input.

D18.followup: APPLIED IN CODE (TensorAccessorArgs appended LAST as compile-time args in both dataflow kernels) but UNMEASURED, because a device-kernel-duration bench structurally CANNOT see it — the lever moves address-gen code and program-cache behaviour, not kernel ns. To close it: add a runtime-accessor-args arm (TensorAccessorArgs(..., ArgConfig::Runtime) plus the <cta, crta> kernel form) and compare dispatch time, or diff ttnn.compute_program_descriptor_hash. D18.reason: Predicted ~0 on device kernel time; the payoff is dispatch/program-cache, which tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/tilize/test_tilize.py::test_tilize_program_cache_hit exercises together with D19. OBSERVED: a probe (tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/tilize/probes/probe_002.py) shows num_program_cache_entries 1 -> 1 across two identical-spec calls with identity intact on both, so the CT/RT split does cache as intended — but that is a dispatch observation, not the ns counterfactual this status would need.

D20.reason: Refinement 4 lands the data path this row was deferred FOR (its own follow-up named A3c). `plan_placement` now selects between four schemes (resident / crossover / reshard / streamed) and, inside the reshard, `reshard_direction_is_pull` selects WHICH SIDE holds the resident block. That second selector is the measured one: the two directions have OPPOSITE signs on geometries that differ only in which side has more cores, so neither can be a global default. Measured on [1,1,1024,1024] bf16 L1->L1, off-arm = the direction the gate did NOT pick: banded WIDTH(1024,128)@8 -> HEIGHT(128,1024)@8 picks push, 22,843 vs 35,594 ns forced pull (1.558x); whole-row HEIGHT(256,1024)@4 -> HEIGHT(128,1024)@8 picks pull, 15,815 vs 25,266 ns forced push (1.598x). Reversing the second pair reverses the winner, which is what proves the gate is selecting a regime rather than expressing a preference.

measured.note: bench shape `reshard` (WIDTH (1024,128)@8 -> HEIGHT (128,1024)@8, L1->L1); off-arm = levers=dict(reshard_pull=1), i.e. forcing op_design 4.3's pull on a geometry the gate sends the other way. The forced-push arm reproduces the shipped number (22,382 ns), which is what shows the gate picked it. The mirror shape `reshard_rowwise` (HEIGHT (256,1024)@4 -> HEIGHT (128,1024)@8) carries the OPPOSITE sign: 15,717 ns shipped (pull, forced-pull 15,547) vs 25,225 ns at levers=dict(reshard_pull=0).

D21.reason: The row's own follow-up asked: does TensorAccessor already specialize the address arithmetic? MEASURED: yes. A hand-rolled replacement — one running address per bank phase, advanced by a stride derived from two real accessor calls, so a block costs bank_period+1 accessor calls instead of tile_h — is 1.078x/1.103x SLOWER on the two smallest shapes, 1.055x on tall_narrow, 1.005x on the square, in the natural issue order (an earlier bank-phase-ordered version was worse still, see B13). The accessor's divisions are by a COMPILE-TIME bank count baked through TensorAccessorArgs, so the compiler already turns them into a multiply-shift; the address table's own array, branch and probe call cost more than they save. Kept as a live knob at the byte-identical default FAST_ADDRGEN = 0, with both bench arms (lever_r6_addrgen_off / lever_r6_addrgen_force) and both values pinned exact.

measured.note: on = fast_addrgen forced, off = shipped default (the accessor per stick).
